      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2(Disk #4);
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  Letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length... Please ask if  you
welcome  direct   correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Les Tyler, Cheltenham.

There may be others,like me, who
use single-sided, double density
40 track discs with their DISC-
iPLE and/or PLUS D interfaces.
With this arrangement, the disc
capacity is limited to 173K of
memory after the 6656 bytes of
the system file is put on.

I have recently come across some
reversible 5.25 inch discs which
allow both sides to be used in a
single-sided drive system. The
discs have 2 notches instead of
the usual 1, also there are 2
sync holes on each side instead
of 1. To access the 'B' side of
the disc it is only necessary to
remove the disc from the drive,
turn it over and re-insert.

I had been thinking of buying a
new double-sided drive system to
accommodate my growing stock of
discs, but learning of these
reversible discs has changed my
mind, at least for the time
being. There may well be other
suppliers of reversible discs,
but the only one I know of at
the moment is...

  MICROMEDIA COMPUTER SUPPLIES
  FREEPOST, DEPT CA3
  RYDAL MOUNT, BAKER STREET
  POTTERS BAR, HERTS, EN6 3BR

    ...who are very quick indeed
with their service. They do lots
of other things as well, not
really Spectrum-orientated and
will supply a catalogue with
your order, if requested.

The reversible discs cost `9.75
for a box of 10,reducing accord-
ing to quantity, and are fully
guaranteed.I have certainly no
complaints so far to make on
them!


Now for a couple of requests for
assistance and/or information. I
have been quite interested in
the 'MICRO-PROLOG' language
package published way back by
Sinclair Research but have
always been held back from going
too far into it,(a) because it
is only tape-based, and (b) it
uses up a vast amount of the
Spectrum memory, which I have
not yet been able to get round
with a 128K machine.

I would be grateful if there is
anyone could tell me how to
transfer the actual data files
to disc. These appear to be
simply headerless blocks of data
which contain somewhere inside
them the instructions to load
the next data block. I think it
probably boils down to finding
the machine code calls to the
SAVE and LOAD routines in the
ROM but my examinations of the
machine code program have so far
not borne fruit.Any help on this
would be appreciated and I would
be interested to know if there
are others around who have this
package and have got somewhere
with it.

I am also sort-of interested in

the Hi-Soft "C" and "Pascal"
packages, would be interested to
hear the views of anyone who has
tried them and whether they
think the languages are superior
(in the Spectrum sense only, of
course) to Sinclair BASIC, aug-
mented by BETA-BASIC. The hard-
ened computer addict will almost
certainly give a hearty guffaw
at that and say"Well,of course!"
but I'm not so sure when it
comes to home computing. I think
the BASIC we have takes some
beating for simplicity and ease
of use. The principal criticism
is usually that of speed but
this only comes into it when us-
ing moving displays as in arcade
games, etc. or in certain cases
where lengthy and repetitive
calculations are involved.

Anyone who can help can contact
me at...
         119 Ashlands Road,
          Cheltenham,
            Glos. GL51 0DJ,

   ...or by 'phone most evenings
on Cheltenham (0242) 30784 -
always glad for a chat on this
topic !

Cheers in advance !

Thanks Les. I know nothing about
Micro-Prolog but I, too, am a
great supporter of BASIC and, in
particular, Spectrum BASIC. It's
regrettable that in the computer
field,as in other walks of life,
there is so much prejudice and
ignorance.            - Brian

work from the RS232 socket if it
works correctly at present. MGT

systems at all.

To Noel White from Brian


You should be able to transfer
your printer software to drive
by using UNITRANS from Issue 16.
Let me know if you have any
problem.

However,it could be difficult to
use this interface to print out
OUTLET text because the software
may use the same memory address-
es that some of our programs
use. If you want to try, alter
line 1415 in the CONTENTS BASIC
to initialize your interface to
print control codes then alter
line 1420 to switch them off.
Both lines must have a RETURN at
the end. If you don't know how

then just try putting RETURN
only at those lines - you may
then get some print-out even if
the margin is not set properly.
To use this, select the KEMPSTON
E option.

Other OUTLET programs may vary
but the most common line to
initialize your printer is at
9884 and adjust any control
codes at 9895 if necessary. You
should then use the USER option
to print. Each program may be
slightly different so unless you
have some grasp of BASIC you may
find it difficult. Regrettably,
it is impossible for OUTLET to
cover all the various interfaces
so we just provide for the most
popular ones.

Alternatively, can you send me
details of your D'ktronics
instructions? Perhaps you can
send a photocopy or lend me your
original? Without this I cannot
advise on your particular inter-
face. With it, I may be able to
help - at least with the main
text files printing.

Since you have an Interface 1
and an HR5 printer with an RS232
I strongly recommend you buy a
cable and then you can use the
Interface 1 option in all OUTLET
programs with no problems. You
can get a cable for `10.95 from
MICROSNIPS, 37 Seaview Road,
Wallasey, Merseyside, L45 4QN

                       - Brian

From Brian to all readers

I'd be interested to hear from
anybody with one of those
printers which have the paper
feed from underneath. I assume
that means there is a tractor
feed BEFORE the paper reaches
the print head. With a normal
tractor feed you can't line up
the top of the top sheet with
the guide but have to wind it on
to the 2nd sheet thus wasting a
sheet. Bad enough if you are
printing out 50 sheets as only
the first one is lost but VERY
wasteful with one-page prints!

I think the DMP series have this
"underneath" paper feed.I'd like
to know how effective it is.
                         - Brian

To Tony Fell from Brian


This is definitely a limitation
of your DOS. You ought to write
to MGT and ask. It may be you
will not need to return your
interface for an update but they
may simply send you the new DOS
on disk.

In the meantime you can do the
following. When a program stops
you can replace CLS# with BORDER
7: PAPER 7: INK 0: BRIGHT 0:OVER
0: INVERSE 0: FLASH 0: CLS

   ...and just remove CLEAR # or
possibly replace it with CLOSE
#3 or CLOSE #4 depending on the
program.

NOTE: You cannot edit the CLEAR
# from the HANDYWIDE REM at line
9977 without corrupting the code
so you should use NEXPIKA from
Issue 16 to find the address of
the CLEAR # and then POKE that
address with 32 which will
replace it with a SPACE.

                    - Brian

involve so much copying to and

to display a menu and LOAD the
text. There is a possibility we
may do general compilations in
the future but these would
almost certainly be OUTLET-sized

To Mr. R. Thomas from Brian


The 32 column margin is only if
you can send in a wordprocessor
file which saves me typing the
whole thing back in! All tapes
and discs are returned and it
does seem a shame for a reader
to type a letter in Tasword,
print it out, send us the print-
out and then I type it back into
Tasword! The reason for the 32
column request is that to re-
format a Tasword file from 64 to
32 column has to be done line by
line which is a bit of a pain at
3.00 a.m. in the morning as our
deadline approaches!You need not
worry about margins if you send
in a printed-out letter only.

To get print-outs from the +3 I
can only suggest you consult the
+3 manual to see how to control
your printer (I think you use
OPEN #3;"P" to initialize) and
alter the lines I've mentioned
in my reply to Noel White in
this issue. I regret that it is
just impossible to cover all
interfaces, particularly when we
do not have the hardware.

COL80 (Issue 18) may be the best
thing to convert first as it can
LOAD and print text files from
any issue (NOT text instructions
BUILT-IN to programs of course)

                      - Brian

From Chris Oliver,  Staffs.

A bug has appeared in "Cat-Kit"
in OUTLET 17 which only came to
light when my original "$" char
was replaced by "EDIT" as the
dump to disc control. A definite
improvement, but unfortunately
upsets other parts of the prog.

Don't despair, all is remedied
by simply adding a line:-

118 IF i$=e$ THEN LET e$=CHR$240
: LET i$=e$

This substitutes a safe high
value for use as the end of
string marker, thus avoiding the
problem which was caused by the
routine mistaking screen

position values for the marker.

To complete the repair, insert
into the rework option at line
2030 ...:LET e$=CHR$ 7:... (or
whatever value was initially
selected in line 20). Chris.





My editing - sorry about that
Chris!

By the way, your other notes I
will put in a future DRIVECHAT.
and the comments in your 12th
Jan. letter noted.
                       - Brian

From Les Tyler, Cheltenham.

There may be others,like me, who use single-sided, double density 40 track discs with their DISC- iPLE and/or PLUS D interfaces. With this arrangement, the disc capacity is limited to 173K of memory after the 6656 bytes of the system file is put on.

I have recently come across some reversible 5.25 inch discs which allow both sides to be used in a single-sided drive system. The discs have 2 notches instead of the usual 1, also there are 2 sync holes on each side instead of 1. To access the 'B' side of the disc it is only necessary to remove the disc from the drive, turn it over and re-insert.

I had been thinking of buying a new double-sided drive system to accommodate my growing stock of discs, but learning of these reversible discs has changed my mind, at least for the time being. There may well be other suppliers of reversible discs, but the only one I know of at the moment is...

MICROMEDIA COMPUTER SUPPLIES FREEPOST, DEPT CA3 RYDAL MOUNT, BAKER STREET POTTERS BAR, HERTS, EN6 3BR

...who are very quick indeed with their service. They do lots of other things as well, not really Spectrum-orientated and will supply a catalogue with your order, if requested.

The reversible discs cost `9.75 for a box of 10,reducing accord- ing to quantity, and are fully guaranteed.I have certainly no complaints so far to make on them!

Now for a couple of requests for assistance and/or information. I have been quite interested in the 'MICRO-PROLOG' language package published way back by Sinclair Research but have always been held back from going too far into it,(a) because it is only tape-based, and (b) it uses up a vast amount of the Spectrum memory, which I have not yet been able to get round with a 128K machine.

These appear to be simply headerless blocks of data which contain somewhere inside them the instructions to load the next data block. I am also sort-of interested in

the Hi-Soft "C" and "Pascal" packages, would be interested to hear the views of anyone who has tried them and whether they think the languages are superior (in the Spectrum sense only, of course) to Sinclair BASIC, aug- mented by BETA-BASIC. The hard- ened computer addict will almost certainly give a hearty guffaw at that and say"Well,of course!" but I'm not so sure when it comes to home computing. I think the BASIC we have takes some beating for simplicity and ease of use. The principal criticism is usually that of speed but this only comes into it when us- ing moving displays as in arcade games, etc. or in certain cases where lengthy and repetitive calculations are involved.

Anyone who can help can contact me at... 119 Ashlands Road, Cheltenham, Glos. GL51 0DJ,

...or by 'phone most evenings on Cheltenham (0242) 30784 - always glad for a chat on this topic !

Cheers in advance !

Thanks Les. I know nothing about Micro-Prolog but I, too, am a great supporter of BASIC and, in particular, Spectrum BASIC. It's regrettable that in the computer field,as in other walks of life, there is so much prejudice and ignorance.            - Brian
